bihar_raw_news.title: State govt to launch campaign from Dec 1 encouraging voluntary contributions to electricity subsidy
bihar_raw_news.content: State govt to launch campaign from Dec 1 encouraging voluntary contributions to electricity subsidy: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary ANI | Updated: Nov 08, 2026 14:05 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [India], November 8 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Sunday announced that the State government will launch a campaign starting December 1 to encourage those who wish to willingly contribute toward the electricity subsidy. Speaking to the reporters, Choudhary extended his heartfelt Diwali greetings and best wishes to the people of the state, expressing hope that Bihar will march forward on the path of prosperity with greater strength. He emphasised the impact of the free electricity scheme, noting that it is illuminating homes across the state. Under this program, 1.92 crore families, spanning diverse economic backgrounds, are receiving 125 units of free electricity, with the government providing approximately Rs 10,000 annually in electricity subsidies per family. "I extend my heartfelt Diwali greetings and best wishes to the people of Bihar . I hope Bihar moves forward on the path of prosperity with greater strength. Under the NDA government's free electricity scheme, lamps are being lit in the homes of poor families. In fact, 1.92 crore families, whether rich or poor, are receiving 125 units of free electricity. We have also made an appeal regarding voluntary contributions. From December 1, we will launch a campaign encouraging those who wish to voluntarily contribute towards the electricity subsidy. Just as the Prime Minister appealed to people to voluntarily give up their LPG subsidies, we are making a similar appeal. The government provides electricity subsidies worth approximately Rs 10,000 annually to each family," he said. He further noted that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit Bihar on November 21 to mark the completion of one year of the NDA government in the state. "One year of the NDA government is about to be completed. We have invited the Prime Minister to Bihar on this occasion. The NDA is working together with complete unity. During the Prime Minister's visit, several announcements and MoUs are expected. Many industrialists are interested in coming to Bihar , and they will also participate in the programme," he said. The Chief Minister commended PM Modi’s recent visit to Bastar , Chhattisgarh, where the Prime Minister celebrated Diwali alongside security forces. "He regularly spends time with soldiers at the borders, and under his leadership, the country has also achieved the goal of becoming Naxal-free. It is a matter of great pride that the Prime Minister personally visited a place like Bastar to celebrate Diwali with our soldiers. I congratulate the Prime Minister, all our soldiers and members of the police forces on this occasion," he said. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Announces 83-km Ganga Riverfront Road Between Munger and Bhagalpur
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Announces 83-km Ganga Riverfront Road Between Munger and Bhagalpur Breaking News Bihar Announces 83-km Ganga Riverfront Road Between Munger and Bhagalpur By Tenzin Choden November 8, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has announced that work will begin on an approximately 83-km Ganga riverfront road between Munger and Bhagalpur, linking the project to improved regional transport and development opportunities along the river corridor. Choudhary made the announcement while inaugurating the Munger Deepotsav programme at the Shri Shri 108 Badi Durga Maharani Mandir in Kalyanpur, under Bariarpur block of Munger district, on Saturday. The event, organised by Youth Club Kalyanpur on the eve of Diwali, featured the simultaneous lighting of 11,11,111 lamps. According to the report, the chief minister said the proposed road would improve transport facilities in the region and open up new possibilities for development. The announcement did not provide details on the project’s estimated cost, alignment, land requirement, executing agency, construction schedule or funding structure. The road proposal was presented in the context of the challenges faced by settlements and farmers along the Ganga. Choudhary referred to recurring floods and crop losses, saying that water from the Nepal Tarai region and the Sone river merges into the Ganga around Dussehra and contributes to flooding in several areas. He said better management and use of Ganga water would be important for farmers. The chief minister also referred to an agreement signed on November 2 with Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari, although the report does not specify whether that agreement directly covers the announced riverfront road, its financing, flood-control works or another water-management intervention. The proposed road would connect two important urban centres in eastern Bihar, but its practical impact will depend on how the alignment is designed and how it interacts with flood-prone areas, agricultural land and existing road infrastructure. No technical details about bridges, embankments, drainage systems or flood-resilient construction standards were provided in the announcement. The chief minister made the infrastructure announcement alongside a broader statement on employment and economic development. He said the state government was working towards creating a system by 2030 in which people from Bihar would not be forced to migrate outside the state for work. He said the government aimed to expand opportunities for jobs, business and self-employment within Bihar. The Munger Deepotsav programme itself was described as a historic celebration for Bihar, with more than 11 lakh lamps lit at one location. Before attending the event, Choudhary offered prayers and performed puja at the Badi Durga Maharani Mandir. The next formal milestones for the Ganga riverfront road will be the release of its alignment, project cost, implementing authority, land and environmental requirements, and construction timeline. The supplied report does not state when physical work is expected to begin beyond the chief minister’s announcement that it will start. national_raw_news.content: The festival of light, Deepawali, is being celebrated with religious fervour and gaiety across the country and abroad. President Droupadi Murmu has extended Diwali greetings to Indians at home and abroad. In her message, she said the festival symbolises the victory of virtue over negativity and marks the end of suffering and the beginning of a joyful and prosperous life. The President has also urged people to protect the environment, promote harmony and contribute towards building a Viksit Bharat. She also wished every citizen good health, happiness and prosperity. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan has greeted fellow citizens and people across the world on the occasion of Diwali. In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan said, Diwali celebrates the universal triumph of light over darkness, good over evil and truth over falsehood, reminding people of the eternal ideal of Satyamev Jayate – Truth Alone Triumphs. He hoped that this Diwali will bring happiness, peace and prosperity to every home and strengthen the bonds of unity and harmony. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will continue his tradition of celebrating Diwali with the brave personnel of the Armed Forces. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has also greeted everyone on the occasion of Diwali. In a social media post this morning, the Prime Minister said, the festival symbolises resolve against darkness. Prime Minister Modi also shared a video message on social media. He said, the festival of lights illuminates the nation and reflects the resolve to overcome darkness. He wished everyone happiness, peace and prosperity.

national_raw_news.title: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh stresses highest operational readiness amid evolving security threats
national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has urged the armed forces to maintain the highest level of operational readiness, stressing the need to strengthen domain awareness, cyber resilience and information integrity amid evolving security challenges. Addressing Indian Air Force (IAF) personnel at Air Force Station Bagdogra in West Bengal on the eve of Diwali, Mr Singh said, modern warfare has expanded beyond conventional border conflicts to include asymmetric warfare, proxy conflicts, cyberattacks, drone swarms and information operations. He cautioned that adversaries were increasingly exploiting vulnerabilities through misleading social media campaigns aimed at creating distrust among local communities and security personnel. The Defence Minister emphasised that military personnel must play a wider role in countering such threats by maintaining public trust and engaging with local communities. Referring to the Cabinet’s approval of the ‘Second Tour of Duty’ for Agniveers, the Defence Minister said the initiative would offer them another opportunity to serve the nation. He said all Agniveers would be eligible for enrolment as regular soldiers after completing their two-year engagement, subject to their willingness and prescribed selection criteria. Calling the decision a significant Diwali gift, the Defence Minister reiterated the government’s commitment to the welfare of defence personnel and their families. He also extended Diwali greetings to the Air Warriors and their families, acknowledging the sacrifices of personnel serving away from home during festivals and appreciating the support extended by their families. Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Air Officer Commanding of Air Force Station Bagdogra Air Commodore Manish Sharma and other senior IAF officials attended the event. Describing Bagdogra as a strategically important location for India’s security framework, particularly in the Northeast, Singh praised the Air Warriors for their dedication and said their preparedness was vital to regional stability. Highlighting the government’s push for ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’, Mr Singh acknowledged the contribution of Indian start-ups and industries to the development of drones, anti-drone systems and advanced military equipment. He urged the forces to embrace indigenous technologies and strengthen their capabilities in drone operations and cybersecurity.

national_raw_news.title: Petroleum Ministry says E20 petrol across India meets prescribed quality standards
national_raw_news.content: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has reaffirmed the claim that E20 petrol supplied by public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs) across the country, including Karnataka, conforms to the prescribed quality standards. It noted that E20 petrol supplied by the three OMCs conforms to IS 17021, the Bureau of Indian Standards specification for ethanol-blended motor gasoline. The Ministry rejected the claims of Karnataka Government that fuel sold at certain retail outlets in the state contains excessive ethanol. The Ministry said that 893 samples collected across 27 States and Union Territories, including 56 from Karnataka, meet the prescribed specifications. The Ministry added that all 56 samples tested in Karnataka conform to IS 17021 specifications, with ethanol content ranging from 19 to 20 per cent. Earlier, the three oil marketing companies, Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation, had clarified that the claims, as reported, were not supported by tests conducted in accordance with the prescribed statutory and technical procedures. In view of the concerns raised, the three OMCs have requested the Karnataka Government to share the complete sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports and details of the test methodology adopted for the reported findings. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas said that the OMCs maintain established quality assurance systems across their supply and distribution networks to ensure that blended fuel meets the applicable BIS specifications before reaching consumers.

national_raw_news.title: Shyama Puja, also known as Kali Puja, celebrated across West Bengal with devotion
national_raw_news.content: In West Bengal, Shyama Puja, popularly known as Kali Puja, is being celebrated today across West Bengal and several parts of the country with traditional fervour and devotion. The festival coincides with Diwali in many parts of the country. From magnificent community pandals to age-old temples and household shrines, preparations are complete to welcome Goddess Shyama, the powerful manifestation of divine feminine energy. The festival is observed on the new moon night of the Hindu month of Kartik, following traditional rituals and religious customs. Some of Bengal’s most revered Kali temples are witnessing special arrangements for the occasion. The Dakshineswar Bhavatarini Temple, closely associated with the spiritual legacy of Sri Ramakrishna Paramahansa, the historic Kalighat Kali Temple, Tarapith and Adyapeath are among the major centres of attraction. Special puja arrangements have also been made at the ancestral home of saint-poet Ramprasad Sen in Halisahar, Karunamoyee Kalibari, Firingi Kalibari and Thanthania Kalibari in Kolkata. The historic Hanseswari Temple at Bansberia in Hooghly district, the famous Boro Maa Kali Puja in Naihati and the Kali temple at Kankalitala, one of the revered Shakti Peethas, are also preparing to receive large numbers of devotees. As Bengal celebrates the triumph of divine power over evil, the night of Amavasya is transformed into a celebration of light, faith and devotion.

national_raw_news.title: Global leaders and diplomats extend greetings on Diwali
national_raw_news.content: The festival of lights, Diwali, will be celebrated tomorrow, marking the triumph of good over evil. Ahead of the celebrations, wishes have begun pouring in from world leaders and diplomats across the globe, including those serving in India. UAE Vice President and Ruler of Dubai, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, extended his Diwali greetings to people celebrating the festival in the United Arab Emirates and around the world. In a post on X, he wished that the festival of lights would bring peace, hope and goodness, while filling people’s lives with safety, happiness and prosperity. European Union Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recalled his first Diwali experience in the country. Sharing his thoughts on X, he described it as a beautiful experience, with lights illuminating every corner. The Embassy of the Republic of Korea in India organised a special diya-decoration workshop to mark the festivities. Norwegian Ambassador to India, May-Elin Stener, shared a video on X extending her Diwali wishes. She noted that although the celebrations were being held within the Embassy premises, the festive greetings and spirit extended far beyond its walls. Germany’s Ambassador to India and Bhutan also conveyed his wishes on the occasion. Denmark’s Ambassador to India, Rasmus Abildgaard Kristensen, highlighted the significance of the festival, saying that even the smallest light can make a big difference. The Embassy of Japan in India also joined the celebrations by hosting a festive lunch. Earlier, US President Donald Trump took part in a ceremonial diya-lighting event at the White House to mark Diwali. The celebration brought together prominent members of the Indian-American community. India’s Ambassador to the United States, Vinay Kwatra, was also present at the ceremony held in the Oval Office. In another significant development, governors of five US states celebrated Diwali at official venues for the first time. The celebrations, held in Idaho, Nebraska, Montana, North Dakota and Washington states.

national_raw_news.title: President, Prime Minister extend greetings on auspicious occasion of Diwali
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has extended her greetings to all Indians living in India and abroad on the eve of Diwali today. In a message, the President said that the festival of Diwali marks the victory of virtues over negative tendencies. She added that the festival also signifies the end of suffering and the beginning of a joyful and prosperous life. She said that on this occasion, people worship Lord Ganesh for auspicious beginnings and well-being, and Goddess Mahalakshmi for prosperity. President Murmu also wished for good health, happiness and prosperity of every citizen of the country. She also urged everyone preserves the environment, live with harmony. The President also appealed to the youth to contribute in building a Viksit Bharat. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also extended his greetings on the occassion of Diwali. Sharing a video message on social media, Mr Modi said that the festival of lights illuminates the entire country and reflects the resolve to overcome darkness. He wished that the festival and the times ahead bring happiness, peace and prosperity to everyone. The Prime Minister further said he celebrates Diwali with great enthusiasm and that, as in previous years, he would continue the tradition of celebrating the festival with the brave soldiers of the country. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has extended his greetings to the citizens for Deepavali, Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj.
